title: Reported speech: statements
summary: Lùi thì, đổi đại từ và dùng say/tell đúng — nền tảng để trích dẫn nguồn trong Writing Task 2.
whyItMatters: Trong Task 2 bạn liên tục phải trích ý kiến người khác: *Critics argue that...*, *The report claimed that...*. Sai thì khi tường thuật khiến người đọc hiểu sai thời điểm của sự việc, còn lẫn *say* và *tell* là lỗi mà giám khảo xếp vào nhóm lỗi cơ bản — rất khó bù bằng từ vựng đẹp.

sections.heading: The one-step backshift
body: When the reporting verb is past (*said*, *told*, *argued*), the verb inside the report usually moves **one step back** in time. The shift is mechanical: present to past, present perfect to past perfect, will to would, can to could.

Past simple is the exception. It can stay as it is (*He said he woke up late*) or become past perfect (*He said he had woken up late*). Both are correct. Choose the past perfect when the order of events would otherwise be unclear, and the past simple when the report is short and the sequence is obvious.
The backshift is not decoration: it tells the reader that the words were spoken before now. Drop it and the sentence claims the situation is still true.

rows: They said they were moving house.
She said she had lost her phone.
He said he would call me.
He said I had to wear a helmet.
He said he woke up late. / he had woken up late.

sections.heading: say and tell: one takes a person, the other does not
body: **tell** must be followed by the person you are talking to: *She told me that she was leaving.* **say** cannot take that person directly — you need **to**: *She said to me that she was leaving.* The compressed form *She said me* does not exist in English.

This is the single most common reported-speech error among Vietnamese learners, because *nói tôi* maps word for word onto *said me*. Train the pair until it is automatic: **tell somebody**, **say something (to somebody)**.
**that** is optional after both verbs. Leaving it out is normal in speech and increasingly common in academic prose; keeping it makes long sentences easier to parse.

examples.right: The manager told us that the deadline had been moved.
examples.wrong: The manager said us that the deadline had been moved.

examples.right: She said that she would send the file.
examples.wrong: She told that she would send the file.

examples.right: He said goodbye to everyone and left.
examples.note: Fixed phrase **say goodbye to somebody** — do not replace *said* with *told*.

sections.heading: When the verb does not move back
body: No backshift is needed when the situation is **still true** at the moment of reporting: *Paul said his new job is boring* (he still works there and still finds it boring). Backshifting is also optional, never wrong — *Paul said his new job was boring* is equally acceptable.

Backshift becomes obligatory when the situation has clearly changed. If Rachel told you that Joe was in hospital, and you then meet Joe in the street, you say *Rachel said you were in hospital* — present tense would be absurd.
General truths and permanent facts normally stay in the present: *The teacher told us that water boils at 100°C.*

examples.right: Helen told me she wants to study in Canada next year.
examples.note: She still wants to go, so the present is natural.

examples.right: Helen told me she wanted to study in Canada next year.
examples.note: Also correct; the backshift is always available.

examples.right: He said he had to leave immediately — and he did.
examples.wrong: He said he has to leave immediately — and he did.
examples.note: Once the moment has passed, the past form is required.

sections.heading: Pronouns, time and place shift too
body: Reported speech re-centres the sentence on the reporter, so pronouns, time expressions and place words move as well: *I* becomes *he/she*, *my* becomes *his/her*, *here* becomes *there*, *tomorrow* becomes *the next day*.
The shift depends on **when and where you report**, not on a fixed rule. If you report the same day in the same city, *today* and *here* can stay. If time has passed, they must move.

Academic writing needs very little of this, because citations are usually about ideas rather than about a conversation happening here and now. Keep the full apparatus for narrative writing and Speaking Part 2.

rows: the next day / the following day
the day before / the previous day
the week before / the previous week

sections.heading: Reporting sources in IELTS Writing
body: Task 2 does not require real citations, but it does reward the grammar of attribution: *Nguyen (2021) found that...*, *Several studies have shown that...*, *Critics of the policy argue that...*.

Note the tense pattern in academic reporting: a study that is finished takes the past (*The survey found that...*), while a body of knowledge still current takes the present perfect (*Research has consistently shown that...*). Both are correct; mixing them randomly inside one paragraph is not.
Avoid the Vietnamese habit of reporting an opinion and then restating it in the same sentence (*According to him, he said that...*). One reporting verb is enough.

examples.right: The authors conclude that subsidies have little effect on demand.
examples.note: Present tense for a conclusion still standing.

examples.right: In 2019 the committee reported that the scheme had failed.
examples.note: Past reporting verb plus past perfect for the earlier failure.

examples.right: Economists have argued that rent controls reduce supply.
examples.wrong: Economists argued that rent controls have reduced supply since 2010.
examples.note: The second clause needs a consistent time frame once the reporting verb is past.

commonMistakes.wrong: He said me that he was tired.
commonMistakes.right: He told me that he was tired.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *nói tôi* dịch thẳng thành *said me*, nhưng **say** không nhận người nghe trực tiếp. Dùng **tell + người** hoặc **say to + người**.

commonMistakes.wrong: She told that she would be late.
commonMistakes.right: She said that she would be late. / She told me that she would be late.
commonMistakes.why: **tell** bắt buộc phải có tân ngữ chỉ người. Thiếu *me/us/him* là câu sai ngữ pháp, không phải văn phong.

commonMistakes.wrong: He said that he will help us.
commonMistakes.right: He said that he would help us.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt không lùi thì trong câu tường thuật (*anh ấy nói anh ấy sẽ giúp*), nên người học giữ nguyên *will*. Động từ tường thuật ở quá khứ kéo theo **will → would**.

commonMistakes.wrong: She said she has finished the report.
commonMistakes.right: She said she had finished the report.
commonMistakes.why: Hiện tại hoàn thành lùi thành **quá khứ hoàn thành** để cho thấy việc hoàn thành xảy ra trước lúc nói.

commonMistakes.wrong: He said he would meet me here tomorrow.
commonMistakes.right: He said he would meet me there the next day.
commonMistakes.why: Khi tường thuật ở thời điểm/địa điểm khác, *here* thành **there** và *tomorrow* thành **the next day**. Giữ nguyên chỉ đúng khi bạn thuật lại ngay tại chỗ, cùng ngày.

ieltsTips: Dùng `X argues that` / `X claims that` ở thì hiện tại khi trích một quan điểm còn hiệu lực — đây là mẫu câu an toàn nhất trong Task 2.
Khi trích số liệu từ một nghiên cứu đã xong, dùng quá khứ: `The 2020 survey found that 62% of respondents...`
Đừng tường thuật rồi nhắc lại: `According to Nguyen, he said that...` là lỗi lặp. Chọn một trong hai cấu trúc.
Trong Speaking Part 3, dùng `I read somewhere that...` hoặc `A friend told me that...` để kể nguồn — nhớ lùi thì cho đúng.

exercises.question: Anna ___ me that she had applied for a scholarship.
exercises.explanation: Có tân ngữ *me* nên phải dùng **tell**: *told me that*.

exercises.question: Tom said he ___ finish the assignment by Friday.
exercises.explanation: Động từ tường thuật *said* ở quá khứ → **will thành would**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: She said me that she was busy.
She told that she was busy.
She told me that she was busy.
She said to that she was busy.
exercises.explanation: Chỉ **tell + người + (that)** là đúng; *say* cần *to* trước người nghe.

exercises.question: The researcher said the data ___ collected over six months.
exercises.explanation: Việc thu thập xảy ra trước lúc phát biểu → hiện tại hoàn thành lùi thành **quá khứ hoàn thành**.

exercises.question: He said he ___ the answer, but he was wrong.
exercises.explanation: Câu kể lại một trạng thái trong quá khứ, không còn đúng nữa → **knew**.

exercises.question: My tutor ___ (tell) me that my essay needed a clearer thesis statement.
She said she ___ (can) speak three languages fluently.
exercises.explanation: **can** lùi thành **could** sau động từ tường thuật ở quá khứ.

exercises.question: They said they ___ (be) planning to move to Ha Noi the following month.
The doctor said I ___ (must) rest for at least a week.
exercises.explanation: **must** trong câu tường thuật quá khứ thường chuyển thành **had to**.

exercises.question: He said he ___ (lose) his passport the week before.
exercises.explanation: Sự việc xảy ra trước thời điểm tường thuật → quá khứ hoàn thành **had lost**.
